uk.title: UK Time / British Time
uk.p1: UK Time covers England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.
uk.p2: The UK is in the Western European time zone. Like many European countries, Daylight Saving Time (summer time) is applied in the UK, moving clocks forward by one hour (GMT + 1). After summer time ends, clocks move back one hour to Western European Time (WET) or GMT.

start.title: Summer Time Starts (25 Mar)
start.description: When local standard time reaches Sunday, 25 March 2012, 01:00:00, it is advanced by 1 hour to Sunday, 25 March 2012, 02:00:00 local daylight time.

end.title: Summer Time Ends (28 Oct)
end.description: When local daylight time reaches Sunday, 28 October 2012, 02:00:00, clocks are set back by 1 hour to Sunday, 28 October 2012, 01:00:00 local standard time.

formula.title: Europe Summer Time Formula
formula.forward: Start: Sunday 31 - (((SS * y) / 4) + 4 mod 7); March at 01:00 GMT
formula.backward: End: Sunday 31 - (((SS * y) / 4) + 1 mod 7); October at 01:00 GMT
formula.note: Note: The formula is valid until 2099. y is the year.

us.title: US & Canada Time
us.p1: US & Canada — Eastern Standard Time (EST) / Eastern Daylight Time (EDT)
us.p2: In the US and Canada, this time zone is generally referred to as Eastern Time (ET). Specifically, it is Eastern Standard Time (EST) when standard time is observed (winter), and Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) when daylight saving time is observed (spring, summer, fall).

start.title: Summer Time Starts (2nd Sunday in March)
start.description: When local standard time reaches Sunday, 11 March 2012, 02:00:00, it is advanced by 1 hour to Sunday, 11 March 2012, 03:00:00 local daylight time.

end.title: Summer Time Ends (1st Sunday in November)
end.description: When local daylight time reaches Sunday, 4 November 2012, 02:00:00, clocks are set back by 1 hour to Sunday, 4 November 2012, 01:00:00 local standard time.

formula.forward: Start: 2nd Sunday in March at 02:00 local time
formula.backward: End: 1st Sunday in November at 02:00 local time
